cover.tagline: One spell in, five spells out — a goblin horde that casts itself.
cover.identity: Zada, Hedron Grinder turns every cheap spell that targets only her into a copy for each other creature you control — so a one-mana cantrip aimed at your commander becomes a fistful of cards when the Goblins are out in force. You flood the board with token makers, fuel monster turns with rituals like Battle Hymn and Brightstone Ritual, and convert the frenzy into damage through Impact Tremors, storm payoffs like Grapeshot and Empty the Warrens, and sacrifice engines like Goblin Bombardment. It plays like a tribal aggro deck that suddenly combusts into a storm deck.

how_it_wins:
The table looks at a pile of 1/1 Goblins and files you under "aggro that runs out of gas." Wrong file. Every body you land is a card Zada, Hedron Grinder cashes later: a spell that targets only her gets copied once for each other creature you control, so one red mana on four bodies is five cards (stack 001). Build the board first, hold the cantrip second.

Bodies are the one thing you are never short of. Dragon Fodder, Krenko's Command, Mogg War Marshal, Empty the Warrens and Siege-Gang Commander flood the table, and General Kreat, Searslicer Goblin and Howlsquad Heavy keep adding a token every combat. Krenko, Mob Boss doubles whatever you have — once. His ability taps, nothing here untaps him, and he is not your commander, so a Krenko in the graveyard stays there (stack 004): play him for the burst and never feed him to Skirk Prospector.

Your ramp is the swarm. Battle Hymn pays {R} per creature you control, Brightstone Ritual pays {R} per Goblin on the battlefield, and Skirk Prospector converts any spare token into red mana with nothing on the stack for anyone to answer. The goldfish has you at 5.18 mana on turn six, which is a fine ordinary curve and would never storm anybody out — so stop waiting on lands for your big turn and start counting Goblins.

Then pick your exit before you fire, because you have three and they are not interchangeable. Impact Tremors turns the swarm into damage no blocker touches: eight tokens is 8 to each opponent before you declare an attack (stack 002). Fists of Flame turns the same board into trample and takes a player off 30 in one swing (stack 003). And Haze of Rage with Storm-Kiln Artist simply does not stop (stack 005) — but the loop hits nobody on its own, so decide which of the other two ends the game before you start it.

combo_lines.001: The clause the whole deck stands on runs four words: a copy of a spell isn't cast (CR 707.10). Zada's ability triggers on casting, so her own copies can never trigger her again, and they add nothing to any storm count. What they do is resolve — separately and in full, one per body, the haste and the draw alike. The holding: one red mana and one card buys five cards and a team that can attack. Every single-target cantrip in this list runs on the same clause.
combo_lines.002: Storm reads "copy it for each other spell that was cast before it this turn" (CR 702.40a), and the case turns on one word: cast. Storm's own copies are put onto the stack without ever being cast, so they raise nobody's count — not their own spell's, and not the Grapeshot you fire later in the same turn. The tokens and the damage below are what four resolutions buy. The storm count that follows is what four casts buy. Those are different numbers, and the holding is to count your casts, not your resolutions.
combo_lines.003: Fists of Flame draws first and buffs second, and CR 608.2h decides what that ordering is worth: if an effect requires information from the game, the answer is determined only once, when the effect is applied. So each copy prices its own +1/+0-per-card at its own resolution and never revises it. The buffs land ascending and they are final; nothing grows retroactively. One caution the record insists on, because this math comes out exactly lethal: a player at 0 or less life loses as a state-based action (CR 704.5a), checked after combat damage is dealt — not during.
combo_lines.004: Commander Spellbook files Krenko, Mob Boss with Skirk Prospector and Goblin Warchief as an infinite. The claim rests on CR 903.9a, which lets an owner move a commander out of the graveyard — and the rule says a commander. Yours is Zada. A Krenko put into the graveyard is a card in a graveyard and stays one. The battlefield route closes just as firmly: his ability costs {T}, only untapped permanents can be tapped (CR 701.26a), and nothing here untaps him. The holding: one cast, one activation, storm count one. What the record does affirm is below, and it is still a very good turn.
combo_lines.005: Buyback puts the spell into its owner's hand instead of the graveyard as it resolves (CR 702.27a) — the card, and only the card. The copies never see a hand at all: a copy of a spell in any zone other than the stack ceases to exist (CR 704.5e). That asymmetry is the engine, since every copy still fired magecraft on its way out. Affirmed: iteration k costs four mana and yields k+3 Treasures — mana-positive from the third cast, strictly better after, unbounded. Where the record is silent is the kill: the loop touches no opponent and grants your team neither haste nor evasion.

card_roles.Zada, Hedron Grinder: Every table reads her as a four-mana 3/3 and lets her live — take the gift. Any instant or sorcery aimed at only her is copied once per other creature you control, so cast your cantrip on the turn you have bodies, not the turn you draw it.
card_roles.Crimson Wisps: One mana, one target, one card — and on four bodies it is five cards and a hasted team (stack 001). Hold it until the board is wide; it costs the same either way.
card_roles.Expedite: The same one-mana blueprint: haste plus a card. Point it at Zada and everything you made this turn can attack this turn.
card_roles.Renegade Tactics: A one-mana cantrip that also says "can't block." Copied across the board it strips the table's blockers and refills your hand at once — fire it precombat, every time.
card_roles.Ancestors' Aid: +2/+0, first strike and a Treasure, all off a single target. Copied, that is a team anthem plus one Treasure per body, so cast it before the expensive spell and spend what it makes.
card_roles.Fists of Flame: Your combat finisher: each copy draws, then locks in +1/+0 per card drawn this turn, and everything gains trample (stack 003). Do the arithmetic before you cast — the buffs land ascending and a lone blocker absorbs almost nothing.
card_roles.Wild Ride: +3/+0 and haste for one mana on one target, which Zada turns into a board-wide anthem. It harmonizes back from the graveyard for {4}{R} — less if you tap a creature — so discarding it early costs you nothing.
card_roles.Frontline Heroism: A copy engine that does not need Zada: every spell targeting only one of your creatures makes a hasty Soldier and then copies that spell at the new token. Deploy it before the pivot turn, not during it.
card_roles.Dragon Fodder: Two bodies for two mana — which is two more copies from every cantrip and two more Impact Tremors triggers. This is a turn-two play, not a storm-turn play.
card_roles.Krenko's Command: The identical two-for-two. Run these out early; the copies they enable later are worth far more than the one storm count they add on the big turn.
card_roles.Empty the Warrens: The storm payoff (stack 002). Cast three cheap spells first — that is the entire difference between four tokens and eight, and under Impact Tremors it is also the difference between 4 and 8 damage to every opponent.
card_roles.Mogg War Marshal: Two bodies now and one more when it dies, for two mana. Let the echo lapse on purpose when you have a sac outlet; the death token is part of the deal.
card_roles.Siege-Gang Commander: Three tokens on arrival and a repeatable {1}{R}, sac-a-Goblin for 2 damage. That second mode is your reach when the ground is gummed up — spend leftover tokens at faces.
card_roles.Siege-Gang Lieutenant: Two hasty tokens at the beginning of every one of your combats, as long as you control Zada. That is a second reason to protect her that has nothing to do with copying spells.
card_roles.General Kreat, the Boltbringer: A free attacking token whenever your Goblins attack, and 1 damage to each opponent whenever another creature of yours enters. On a storm turn he is a second Impact Tremors — count him in your damage math.
card_roles.Searslicer Goblin: A free token at every end step you attacked. Attack with something, even a lone 1/1 you can afford to lose.
card_roles.Howlsquad Heavy: Haste for your other Goblins and a free attacking token each combat. The tap-for-{R}-per-Goblin line needs max speed, so treat the mana as a bonus and the haste as the reason he is here.
card_roles.Redcap Gutter-Dweller: Menace, two Rat tokens on entry, and an upkeep sacrifice that grows him and exiles you a card to play. Feed it the token you were going to sacrifice anyway.
card_roles.Impulsive Pilferer: A one-mana Goblin that leaves a Treasure when it dies — sacrifice it to Prospector or Bombardment and you have turned a body into two mana. Encore it from the graveyard for {3}{R} when the board is empty.
card_roles.Goblin Bushwhacker: Kick it for the extra {R} and the whole team gets +1/+0 and haste. That is your out-of-nowhere alpha strike; unkicked it is a 1/1 that adds a cast to your count.
card_roles.Goblin Chieftain: +1/+1 and haste for every other Goblin. Haste is the word that matters: tokens made this turn swing this turn.
card_roles.Goblin Warchief: Goblin spells cost {1} less and your Goblins have haste — he is exactly why Krenko costs {1}{R}{R} and activates the turn he lands (stack 004). Play him before the wave, not after.
card_roles.Goblin Trashmaster: An anthem for the swarm plus a repeatable sacrifice-a-Goblin to destroy an artifact. Against a rocks-and-equipment table he is removal you get to use every single turn.
card_roles.Rundvelt Hordemaster: +1/+1 to your other Goblins, and every Goblin death exiles the top card — Goblin creature cards are castable until end of your next turn. With him out, sacrifice freely.
card_roles.Quest for the Goblin Lord: One mana, and after five Goblins have entered the whole team gets +2/+0. A single Empty the Warrens or one Krenko activation fills it in one go, so play it early and let the swarm do the work.
card_roles.Goblin Lackey: Connect once and a Goblin permanent walks out of your hand for free. Send him at the empty seat on turn two; the free Siege-Gang Commander is not a fantasy on an open board.
card_roles.Goblin Matron: Tutors any Goblin card straight to hand. Default to whichever engine piece is missing — Skirk Prospector for mana, Goblin Warchief for the discount, Krenko for bodies.
card_roles.Gempalm Incinerator: Cycle it for {1}{R} to draw a card and deal damage equal to the number of Goblins on the battlefield. Know the trap: cycling is an ability, not a cast, so it adds nothing to your storm count — take the removal anyway.
card_roles.Goblin Dark-Dwellers: Menace, and on entry he casts an instant or sorcery of mana value 3 or less from your graveyard for free. Aim him at a spent ritual like Seething Song mid-storm-turn, not at a cantrip.
card_roles.Grenzo, Havoc Raiser: Every creature of yours that connects goads something or exiles the top of that player's library for you to cast. On a wide board that is several triggers a turn — send the goads at whoever is closest to winning.
card_roles.Broadside Bombardiers: Menace and haste, and once it has attacked you may sacrifice a creature or artifact to deal 2 plus that permanent's mana value anywhere. Attack first — the boast is gated on having attacked, and that ordering is a cost, not a suggestion.
card_roles.Goblin Bombardment: A free, repeatable sac outlet that turns any body into 1 damage at any target. It is your wrath insurance: when the sweeper resolves, the board should already be damage on the stack.
card_roles.Pashalik Mons: 1 damage every time one of your Goblins dies, plus a {3}{R} sacrifice that makes two more. With Bombardment alongside, each token you crack is 2 damage instead of 1.
card_roles.Boggart Shenanigans: 1 damage to a player for every other Goblin of yours that hits the graveyard from the battlefield — and your tokens qualify. Pair it with a sac outlet and a wide board and you have a kill that ignores blockers.
card_roles.Skirk Prospector: Sacrifice a Goblin, add {R}, with nothing on the stack for anyone to answer (stack 004). This is how a board becomes a storm turn — but the mana empties at end of phase, so only crack bodies you are spending right now.
card_roles.Skullclamp: One mana to cast, one to equip, and every 1/1 you clamp dies immediately and draws you two. It is the best draw engine in the deck and the only one a wrath makes better.
card_roles.Battle Hymn: {R} for each creature you control, for two mana. You average 4.07 bodies by turn five, so cast it after your token maker and treat it as a four-mana instant that costs two.
card_roles.Brightstone Ritual: One mana for {R} per Goblin on the battlefield — every Goblin, including the ones across the table. It is the cheapest accelerant you own, so it goes early in the storm turn.
card_roles.Mana Geyser: {R} for each tapped land your opponents control. Fire it on a turn the table has spent itself, never on your own quiet turn five.
card_roles.Seething Song: Three mana in, five out. It nets two and, just as importantly, adds a cast to your storm count on the way through.
card_roles.Ruby Medallion: Every red spell costs {1} less, and 57 cards in this list carry a red pip. On a ten-spell turn that is ten extra mana — deploy it before the turn you plan to go off, not during.
card_roles.Sol Ring: Two colourless on turn one, which makes every {3}{R} payoff in the deck arrive a turn early. Cast it first and never think about it again.
card_roles.Grapeshot: One damage per storm copy, split however you like. It counts only spells you actually cast (stack 002), so it is the last spell of your turn, never the first.
card_roles.Haze of Rage: A team-wide +1/+0 with storm and buyback {2}. With Storm-Kiln Artist it is unbounded (stack 005); without him it is still the best anthem you can cast twice in one turn.
card_roles.Spreading Insurrection: Steal a creature, untap it and give it haste — once for each spell cast before it. Late in a storm turn it takes the table's blockers and points them back at their owners.
card_roles.Storm-Kiln Artist: A Treasure for every instant or sorcery you cast or copy, and Zada's copies count. Four bodies out means one cantrip mints four Treasures — he is the piece that makes stack 005 real, so protect him accordingly.
card_roles.Past in Flames: Flashback for every instant and sorcery in your graveyard. Cast it after the rituals are spent, not before — it is your second storm turn, not your first.
card_roles.Faithless Looting: Two cards for one mana, then discard two, with flashback for {2}{R}. It converts a hand of rituals with no board into a hand with a board.
card_roles.Glimpse the Impossible: Three cards off the top you may play this turn, and whatever you leave behind becomes Eldrazi Spawn that sacrifice for colourless. Cast it early in the turn with mana still up; the cards expire at end step.
card_roles.Witch's Mark: Discard a card, draw two, and hang a Wicked Role on one of your creatures. It is your cheapest way to bin Past in Flames or Wild Ride for a later flashback — treat whether Zada copies it as an open question, not a plan.
card_roles.Idol of Oblivion: Two mana, and then a card every turn you made a token — which is nearly every turn you take. Deploy it early and it pays for itself twice over.
card_roles.Great Train Heist: Spree: {2}{R} untaps your team and adds a combat, {2} gives +1/+0 and first strike, {R} turns combat damage into Treasures. On a wide board the extra-combat mode is a win condition, so save it for the swing that matters.
card_roles.Blasphemous Act: Thirteen damage to every creature, and it costs {1} less per creature on the battlefield — usually {R} at your tables. Your swarm dies too, so cast it when you are behind on board and never when you are ahead.
card_roles.Vandalblast: One mana to break their best rock, {4}{R} overloaded to break all of them and none of yours. Hold it for the artifact deck instead of trading it for a Sol Ring on turn three.
card_roles.Swiftfoot Boots: Hexproof and haste for three mana total. Zada with hexproof is the difference between the pivot turn happening and the pivot turn getting removed in response.
card_roles.Throne of Eldraine: Four mana of your chosen colour — spells only. Know exactly what that excludes: it cannot pay Skullclamp's equip, Goblin Burrows' pump, or even Throne's own draw-two. Cast with it, never activate.
card_roles.Reliquary Tower: No maximum hand size. On the turn a copied cantrip draws you eight cards, this is the land that lets you keep all eight.
card_roles.War Room: Three mana and one life for a card — mono-red means the life cost is exactly one. Colourless is a small price for a land that draws.
card_roles.Arena of Glory: Enters untapped as long as you control a Mountain, which 22 of your lands are. Its exert line turns {R} into {R}{R} with haste attached to a creature spell — save that for Krenko or Siege-Gang Commander.
card_roles.Castle Embereth: A red source with a team pump for {1}{R}{R}. On a board of twenty 1/1s that is a real threat of 20 extra damage, so leave it untapped on the swing turn.
card_roles.Den of the Bugbear: Enters untapped while you have fewer than two other lands, and becomes a 3/2 Goblin for {3}{R} that makes a token when it attacks. It is a body that sweepers do not see coming — animate it after the wrath, not before.
card_roles.Dwarven Mine: Enters untapped once you control three other Mountains and hands you a Dwarf when it does. Play your basics first and this land is a free body.
card_roles.Kher Keep: Colourless mana plus {1}{R} for a 0/1 Kobold. A Kobold is a body: Zada copies at it, Prospector eats it, Skullclamp draws off it.
card_roles.Fountainport: Colourless with three sinks — sacrifice a token to draw, make a Fish, make a Treasure. Late in the game it is where your leftover tokens become cards, one per turn.
card_roles.Goblin Burrows: Colourless mana plus {1}{R} to give a Goblin +2/+0. Use it to win the combat the table thinks you lose.
card_roles.Shinka, the Bloodsoaked Keep: A red source that hands a legendary creature first strike. You run five legendary creatures, so it is live more often than it looks — most usefully on a blocked Zada.
card_roles.Spinerock Knoll: Hideaway 4 on arrival, and you cast the exiled card free once an opponent has taken 7 damage in a turn. Impact Tremors clears that bar on its own, so play this land before the storm turn, not after.
card_roles.Hidden Volcano: A tapped red source that later sacrifices itself for Discover 4. Drop it on a turn where a tapped land costs you nothing, which is most turns before four.
card_roles.Forgotten Cave: Enters tapped and cycles for {R} when you are flooded. That is the whole job and it does it well.
card_roles.Smoldering Crater: Forgotten Cave's twin with cycling {2}. Land when you need a land, a card when you do not.
card_roles.Mountain: Twenty-two copies, untapped and red every time. They are why 33 of your 36 lands make the only colour you care about — lead with them so your conditional lands enter untapped.
card_roles.Krenko, Mob Boss: One tap, one wave of Goblins equal to your Goblin count, and that is the turn (stack 004). Plan around a single activation, and never sacrifice him to Prospector — he does not come back.
card_roles.Impact Tremors: 1 damage to each opponent for every creature of yours that enters. Eight tokens is 8 a head before you attack (stack 002) — this is how you kill through a wall of blockers, so resolve it before the storm turn.
card_roles.Conspicuous Snoop: Top card revealed, and you may cast Goblin spells from it — 25 of your 64 nonland cards qualify. He also borrows the activated abilities of a Goblin on top, so check what is up there before you tap out.
card_roles.Roaming Throne: Name Goblin and every Goblin creature's triggered ability fires twice — Zada, General Kreat, Pashalik Mons and Searslicer Goblin all qualify, and Impact Tremors does not. Whether a doubled Zada trigger makes a second full set of copies is unsettled; it needs a scenario before you build a turn on it.
card_roles.Moggcatcher: {3} and a tap puts a Goblin permanent from your library straight onto the battlefield. He is a Human, so none of your haste anthems reach him — expect to wait a turn and expect the table to shoot him.
card_roles.Chaos Warp: Your only clean answer to a permanent you cannot otherwise touch — an enchantment, a resolved combo piece, an untargetable threat. Save it for that; do not spend it on a creature you could have blocked.
card_roles.Daring Discovery: Three creatures cannot block, then Discover 4 — and most of this deck costs 4 or less, so the free spell is usually real. Cast it precombat, when the "can't block" half still means something.
card_roles.Goblin Negotiation: X damage to a creature, and every point of excess becomes a 1/1 Goblin. Aim a big X at a small blocker and you have bought removal and a swarm with one card.
card_roles.Sazacap's Brew: It targets a player, so Zada never copies it — that is exactly why it sits in the sideboard rather than the 99. Bring it in when you want instant-speed draw-two and one more cast on the count, and leave it out against graveyard exile.

mulligan:
Most players mulligan hunting for the payoff. You do not have to: Zada waits in the command zone at four mana and gets cast by turn six in 90% of games. Your opening seven does not need a win condition. It needs lands and something that makes Goblins.

Keep three lands — or two plus Sol Ring, Skirk Prospector or Ruby Medallion — alongside a cheap token maker like Dragon Fodder, Krenko's Command, Mogg War Marshal or Searslicer Goblin, and bank a one-mana cantrip for the turn Zada lands. That is the ordinary hand here, not the dream: 79% of first sevens clear the keep rule and the average game costs you a quarter of a mulligan. Keep the ordinary hand.

Ship the hands that are all payoff and no setup. Mana Geyser, Empty the Warrens and Blasphemous Act on two lands is a mulligan every time — rituals need a board and storm needs a spell count. Only 15% of games ever put a storm payoff and a ritual in your hand together, so stop waiting for that seven and take the one that makes bodies on turn two.

Two cards rescue a marginal keep. Faithless Looting and Witch's Mark both trade dead cards for live ones for two mana or less, so a hand with lands, one body and a looter is a keep — snap it off and dig.

One habit for the big turns: the Red Mana and Storm Counter cards in your sideboard carry no rules text, they are table aids. Lay them in front of you before you start a storm turn and track floating mana and casts out loud. Ten-spell turns are precisely where good pilots miscount.
upgrades:
Ten names below, nine of them scouted from the pool and one sitting in the sideboard, and the ordering has nothing to do with fame. The card in first place ranks 13,958th on EDHREC. The card in ninth ranks 76th. What actually sorts this list is how much of each line is already sleeved.

Reiterate is the cleanest arithmetic on it: one card completes three separately flagged infinite lines, and every other piece — Mana Geyser, Seething Song, Ruby Medallion, Storm-Kiln Artist — is already in the 99. Purphoros, God of the Forge makes the opposite case and still earns its slot: it opens no new line at all, it just doubles a rate. The verified Empty the Warrens turn bills 8 a head through Impact Tremors; the entry prices that same turn at 24.

Every infinite named here is flagged, not verified — the status field reads "needs a stack scenario" and means it literally. Worth knowing what that does and does not move: this deck's computed floor is already bracket 4, off a single two-card infinite that assembles at mana value 4, and all ten entries carry a bracket delta of 4 to 4. Jeska's Will is the one Game Changer among them, and it does not shift the floor either.

One channel came back almost empty, which is informative in itself. The obsolescence index finds seven cards in the 99 with a newer lookalike and none of the seven reached the ten. Its tightest match here is 0.9877 — Dragon's Desire against Mana Geyser — and it quietly swaps the denominator from your opponents' tapped lands to your opponents' artifacts, which is a completely different bet. Second tightest is 0.974, Contract Hero against Storm-Kiln Artist: one Treasure when it enters, against one per instant or sorcery cast or copied. That second clause is the entirety of stack 005.
mana_base:
Thirty-six lands across fifteen entries, twenty-two of them Mountains. Eight enter tapped — 22%, inside the usual one-in-three budget, and five of those eight enter tapped no matter what. The colour ledger is the shortest one this magazine prints: pip share 1.00, source share 1.00. Mono-red leaves nothing to arbitrate.

Thirty-three of the thirty-six lands make red, against a target of thirty-six. That target deserves a second look, because it is asking every land in the deck to produce red, and the three that do not are Reliquary Tower, War Room and Fountainport — lands in the list for what they do, not what they tap for. The audit's own phrasing is a yardstick, not a possibility, in a 36-land deck. Lands alone still put red on curve 86.9% of the time.

The demand side is light, which is why 86.9% reads as comfortable rather than alarming. Sixty-nine red pips spread across 57 cards, first needed on turn one, and the heaviest ask anywhere in the deck is {R}{R} — effective pip requirement 2. A list whose worst colour requirement is two red does not need that thirty-sixth source the way a triple-pip deck would.

Rocks and dorks lift the count to 43 sources and the on-curve figure to 96%, and that flatters what the ramp actually is: six rituals, four dorks, one rock, three cost-reducers. Rituals are not sources. They do not add mana per turn, they add mana to one turn, which is the only unit a storm count trades in — Battle Hymn against a mean of 4.07 bodies on turn five is a two-mana instant that hands you about four red. And one source that counts for nothing: Throne of Eldraine adds four, spells-only, so it cannot pay Skullclamp's equip or Goblin Burrows' pump and never appears in the 43.

The turn-by-turn picture is ordinary, and that is the point. Land drops hit 90.0% on turn three, 54.2% on turn six and 38.2% by turn ten; mean available mana runs 3.937 on turn four, 5.182 on turn six and 6.964 on turn ten. Five mana has never stormed anybody out of a game. The base's job is delivering that five reliably — the rituals and the swarm are the multiplier that goes on top of it.
threat_assessment:
The table has already decided what you are. A pile of 1/1s, a red deck, the seat you deal with after the real problems get solved. Let them keep believing it. Your whole early game is spending that belief, and your whole craft is knowing the exact turn it expires.

They can read your clock, so let them. Zada gets cast on turn four in 7,002 of 10,000 goldfish runs — anyone who has faced this deck counts your Mountains and circles that turn, so cast her on curve anyway and let them watch the wrong card. She is a four-mana 3/3 the turn she lands. Pass with mana up you have no intention of spending.

What they cannot read is the board. You average 2.36 bodies on turn three, which looks like two chump blockers and a Prospector, so put them down early and let the read stand. Deploy the token makers first — your early token maker is drawn by turn 3.18 on average, so you have them.

Hold the loud cards until the table's removal has found other homes. Krenko, Storm-Kiln Artist and Conspicuous Snoop all announce something. Snoop in particular shows every opponent your library top for the rest of the game, so play it when the information is worth the attention and not on the turn you draw it.

You flip from ignored to archenemy at two moments, and you choose when both happen. Moment one is Zada untapped, three other bodies, one red open — that is the payload stack 001 verified, five cards and a hasted team for a single {R}. Fire it when sorcery-speed answers are the only answers your opponents have left.

Moment two is Storm-Kiln Artist on your battlefield, four mana up, Haze of Rage in hand. Stack 005 has that loop going mana-positive from the third cast and strictly improving after, so treat the first Haze cast as your commitment point. Never make it into untapped blue.

Informed opponents have a script against you and it is short: kill Storm-Kiln in response to the first magecraft trigger, or answer the Treasures at instant speed. Count their open mana before you cast, not after. Make them run that script with mana they have already spent, and it stops being a script.

Krenko, Mob Boss is the best misinformation you own — play him as one. The combo databases file him with Skirk Prospector and a haste lord as an infinite; stack 004 says it is not one in this deck, because he taps, nothing untaps him, and he is not your commander, so the graveyard keeps him. Cast him for what he actually is: one activation, ten Goblins, 13 hasted power.

So when an opponent burns removal on him because they read the databases instead of the board, take the trade and say nothing. Never spend protection defending a loop you do not have. Never feed him to Prospector expecting him back.

One more discipline before the big turn: do the arithmetic first and count only what you can see. Mana on the battlefield, spells in hand, bodies on board. Cards you might draw are a bonus and never a plan, and a cantrip fired at Zada for two copies of value is a trade available every turn and worth taking on almost none of them.

Go when Impact Tremors or Boggart Shenanigans is down, when Krenko stands untapped beside Prospector, when Spinerock Knoll is set, or when the Haze loop is live. The storm-payoff-plus-ritual hand shows up in 15.2% of goldfish games, so stop waiting on it and win with the engine you assemble in the other 85%.

Then embrace it. The turn you draw five cards in front of three opponents you are the archenemy, and you should be delighted about it — that is the turn they have to answer you or start dying, and you got to pick which turn it was.
matchups:
Every archetype at this table has a plan for a red creature deck. None of them has a plan for a red creature deck that draws five cards for one mana. Sort the seats by that gap and play accordingly.

Start with sweeper control, because it is the matchup most pilots misplay. Your engine is wrath insurance, not a wrath victim — cards in hand and Treasures on the battlefield sit in two zones a creature sweeper cannot reach. So when the wrath is telegraphed at sorcery speed, fire the cantrip engine and bank the draws.

Stack 001 is the whole argument: one red converts your most sweeper-vulnerable board into your least sweeper-vulnerable resources. Do not hold the engine waiting for a lethal that never gets cheaper. Their only instant-speed interaction is a counterspell they would rather save for your kill — so make them spend it on a cantrip.

Keep one token maker in hand at all times and treat Past in Flames as the rebuild button rather than a storm piece. Charge them rent for the wrath itself: Pashalik Mons and Goblin Bombardment turn a dying board into damage on the way out.

Stax and tax pieces attack your arithmetic, not your creatures, so recount your hand under the tax before you commit to anything. A two-spell turn that becomes a one-spell turn has halved your engine. One lock piece is an inconvenience — the second and third are the game, so break the first one early and cheaply.

Name your outs out loud before you need them: Vandalblast, Goblin Trashmaster, Chaos Warp. Sequence to protect the out that answers the piece beating you, not the piece scaring you. You are the beatdown under a lock, so race the assembly and stop hedging.

Take heart, though, because mana denial hurts you less than the table assumes. Ruby Medallion and Goblin Warchief pay the toll, and Battle Hymn and Brightstone Ritual scale off Goblins instead of lands — your land drops are already down to 54% by turn six, so stop budgeting the big turn out of lands.

Even the Haze loop survives a sphere. Redo the math and a two-mana tax pushes the profitable cast out an iteration or two. Delayed is not dead, so keep going.

Aggro and token mirrors are yours on asymmetry, so stop trying to be bigger than them. Gempalm Incinerator cycles to kill their lord and counts their Goblins toward X, so read their board before you name the target. Blasphemous Act is frequently a two-mana sweeper in that pod and you are the only seat built to rebuild from it — hold it as your reset, not your removal.

When you need a mirror-breaker, Krenko is it: one activation, ten Goblins, 13 hasted power, spent as the one-shot stack 004 proved it to be. Then win where blockers do not matter. Impact Tremors and General Kreat drain every opponent without you declaring a single attack, so let the other token deck wear the archenemy hat and thank it for the cover.

Combo tables invert your instincts about holding answers. Your interaction is thin — Chaos Warp, Gempalm Incinerator, Bombardment in response to a trigger — so an answer you hold rots while their board improves. Rank every opponent by combo proximity rather than board presence and spend your one piece of disruption at the decisive moment, not the comfortable one.

Do not plan to out-race a dedicated combo deck. Plan to be the reason their setup turn gets punished: apply pressure so they must tap out into a table that can kill them, and point Grenzo's goads at whoever is closest to going off.

Graveyard hate barely taxes you, so do not play around it. Past in Flames and Wild Ride's harmonize are the only cards in the 99 that want a graveyard, so when a Rest in Peace sits down, write off the rebuild and lean harder on token makers and Skullclamp. That is a matchup you fix by ignoring it.

One counting habit for every one of these seats: stack 002 settles that copies are not casts, so your storm count tracks the spells you cast and nothing else. Count casts out loud on the big turn.

And when someone asks whether you are 'the storm deck', give them the honest answer — a Goblin deck with a very good draw engine. It stays true right up until Storm-Kiln Artist hits the battlefield, and by then the question is not really theirs to ask.
